title: The Museum Switch
subtitle: The frame is right. The painting is not.
briefing: A visiting conservator notices that the varnish on the gallery's best-known portrait is wrong for its age. Analysis confirms the canvas on display is a modern replica of considerable quality. The original was last verified eleven days ago. In between, the painting left its wall exactly once, for scheduled restoration work.
solution: Gregor Melnyk, the restoration technician, made the substitution during the four days the painting was legitimately in his studio. The replica had been painted over eight months from photographs he took during earlier work. The delivery van that looked suspicious belonged to a genuine framing contractor, and the camera gap was a scheduled maintenance window that had been published internally.

topics.studio_days: the painting's time in the studio

suspects.name: Gregor Melnyk
suspects.relation: Had the painting for four days
suspects.motive: Sole unsupervised access to the original, and the skill to copy it.

statements.question: What happened during the four days?
statements.text: Routine consolidation of the lower left quadrant. Nothing else.

statements.question: Whose van was at the loading bay?
statements.text: The framers. They come every month.

statements.question: Why was there a camera gap?
statements.text: Scheduled maintenance. It was on the internal notice board for weeks.

suspects.name: Adele Fournier
suspects.motive: Signed the movement order and holds the only other studio key.

statements.question: What happened during the four days?
statements.text: It was signed in and signed out. I checked it myself on the Friday.

statements.question: Whose van was at the loading bay?
statements.text: Ashfield Framing. They have held our contract for six years.

statements.question: Why was there a camera gap?
statements.text: The upgrade. It was announced. I was in Lyon for all of it.

suspects.name: Tomas Reyes
suspects.motive: In debt, and has been seen photographing works after hours.

statements.question: What happened during the four days?
statements.text: I would not know. Attendants do not go into the studio.

statements.question: Whose van was at the loading bay?
statements.text: There was one I did not recognise on the Wednesday. No livery on it.

statements.question: Why was there a camera gap?
statements.text: Nobody tells me anything about the cameras.

suspects.name: Nell Harkness
suspects.motive: Was disciplined last year for falsifying a loan document.

statements.question: What happened during the four days?
statements.text: In on the Monday, out on the Friday, both signed. I have the sheets.

statements.question: Whose van was at the loading bay?
statements.text: Ashfield Framing, booked and logged. Wednesday, eleven o'clock.

statements.question: Why was there a camera gap?
statements.text: The upgrade window. Published, scheduled, boring.

A framing van uses the loading bay.

hints: The frame was never taken. Ask what that means about where the swap happened.
Two things look suspicious and both have paperwork. Check the paperwork.
A copy that good was not made in four days.
